column4: Pixel-art texture in the style of 1990s Build-engine games (Duke Nukem 3D, Blood, Redneck Rampage): a digitized photograph crudely retouched by hand by a 1996 game artist, flat even lighting, no glow, no bloom, no depth of field, no soft shadows, chunky pixels, a limited muddy palette, low saturation, slightly grimy and imperfect, hard edges, no readable text, no logos, no border, no watermark, no people, no hands. A flat orthographic straight-on view, no perspective, filling the whole 16:9 canvas edge to edge: The front facade of a 1970s Czechoslovak brutalist bowling alley (a village kuzelna) of raw cast concrete: heavy weathered grey concrete panels with dark water stains, rust streaks from the steel anchors and green moss running down from the top edge, crude spray-painted graffiti tags low on the wall, a recessed entrance in the middle with a steel-framed glass double door under a thick cantilevered concrete canopy slab, a long narrow horizontal band of dirty yellowish glass blocks above the door, high across the top an empty dark steel rail where neon letters will hang (no letters), a dark chipped plinth along the bottom. No sky, no ground, no roof, only the wall.
